payload.author: osrshool222
payload.body:
That is a fair concern. I wanted to extend the existing [Expose Bank State plugin](https://runelite.net/plugin-hub/show/expose-bank-state), which already exposes read-only local interface state over localhost.
The additional states are intended for legitimate local integrations such as accessibility tools, companion overlays, stream/control interfaces, and development/testing tools.
The plugin only reads visible RuneLite widgets and exposes the latest snapshot on 127.0.0.1. It does not click, type, move the player, automate actions, or send data to an external server. It also does not expose the character name, coordinates, credentials, or other account data.
I understand that interface-state data could be misused. If preferred, I would be happy to contribute these additions directly to Expose Bank State instead of maintaining a separate plugin, to avoid fragmentation.

payload.author: Jordan-Hn
payload.body:
> Is there a reason you can't just change the scale to a number less than 1? https://github.com/runelite/runelite/wiki/RuneLite-Launcher-Configuration#Scale

Scale lowers the floor but doesn't remove it. --scale=0.5 halves every Java 2D unit, so the 765x503 minimum lands at roughly 383x252 physical pixels, and you still can't drag below that. Changing it means editing launcher config and restarting, rather than just dragging the window.

The results also differ. Scale shrinks the whole client proportionally, sidebar and config panels included, and the game still lays out at 765 logical px, so you get the same view at reduced resolution. This leaves rendering at 1:1 and lowers the minimum instead, so the game reflows its interface for the narrower viewport and text stays at native size.

Different problems: scale is "make everything smaller", this is "let the window be smaller".

payload.author: ConnorFitzgerald17
payload.body:
@Alexsuperfly Flagging a post-merge naming and configuration collision.
 
**Iron Path**, a separate RuneLite plugin and web application added through PR #14932. After both plugins were merged, I noticed that their display names and RuneLite configuration namespaces are effectively identical.

For reference, here is the public chronology:

* The first public Iron Path commit was made on [[August 6, 2026](https://github.com/ConnorFitzgerald17/iron-path-runelite/commit/876beb72fa6c0731459f6ab0c02ba09e40fa2f40)](https://github.com/ConnorFitzgerald17/iron-path-runelite/commit/876beb72fa6c0731459f6ab0c02ba09e40fa2f40).
* The Iron Path Plugin Hub PR, #14932, was opened on August 10.
* The `ironpathosrs.com` domain was registered on August 10.
* This plugin’s first public commit was made on [[August 26, 2026](https://github.com/gabworknestio-beep/ironpath/commit/a3b0339b1334a1e3d8e09a1cedfebe3e0ac6eb0e)](https://github.com/gabworknestio-beep/ironpath/commit/a3b0339b1334a1e3d8e09a1cedfebe3e0ac6eb0e), and its Plugin Hub PR was opened later that day.
* Both submissions were merged on August 27 after being reviewed independently.

The plugins serve different purposes, but RuneLite users now see both **Iron Path** and **IronPath** in the Plugin Hub. More importantly, both plugins use the same `ironpath` configuration group:

* [[Iron Path configuration group](https://github.com/ConnorFitzgerald17/iron-path-runelite/blob/c2241dbbdf367bee5021e4f4e1cbc0d67d20279e/src/main/java/gg/ironpath/IronPathConfig.java#L11)](https://github.com/ConnorFitzgerald17/iron-path-runelite/blob/c2241dbbdf367bee5021e4f4e1cbc0d67d20279e/src/main/java/gg/ironpath/IronPathConfig.java#L11)
* [[IronPath configuration group](https://github.com/gabworknestio-beep/ironpath/blob/0444acdea8986cfdd1d9827a0ff63c3b78d80d41/src/main/java/com/ironpath/IronPathConfig.java#L11)](https://github.com/gabworknestio-beep/ironpath/blob/0444acdea8986cfdd1d9827a0ff63c3b78d80d41/src/main/java/com/ironpath/IronPathConfig.java#L11)

RuneLite stores configuration under the configuration-group namespace. Although the plugins currently use different individual setting keys, sharing the same group creates ambiguity and could cause configuration collisions now or in the future. The nearly identical display names also make it difficult for users to distinguish the existing Iron Path service and its connected plugin from this unrelated progression plugin.

I understand this was likely an accidental naming collision, especially since both plugins were reviewed independently. I am not asking for any functionality to be removed. Would you be willing to update this plugin to use:

1. A clearly distinct display name.
2. A unique `@ConfigGroup` value other than `ironpath`.

Since both plugins were only recently merged, addressing this now should minimize user confusion and reduce the impact of any configuration migration. I’m happy to coordinate on the changes if that would be helpful.

Thank you.

I’ll update the plugin with a unique display name and configuration group. Since both plugins were only just merged, now is definitely the best time to clean this up before more users install them.

I appreciate you reaching out constructively and providing the references and timeline.

payload.author: MikeSpatol
payload.body:
Thanks, both removed. The pin now points at MikeSpatol/follower-buddy@c197039.

The sleep/interrupt lived in the two editor windows' save paths, retrying an atomic rename while the plugin's own reload poll briefly held the file open on Windows. The save now attempts the rename once and falls back to an in-place write on contention, which the loader already tolerates: it keeps its previous rules if a poll catches a torn read and picks up the finished file on the next poll.

payload.author: Wolklaw
payload.body:
Bumped the pin from `2a16b856` to `a652df8`. Not a cosmetic update — the previously pinned build had a bug that made half the plugin silently do nothing, and I would rather it not be reviewed in that state:

- **Live Grand Exchange state never reached the service.** The client sent `POST` to two endpoints the service routes as `PUT`, so every offer-slot and offer-screen write came back `405` and was discarded. It failed quietly because a 4xx is treated as "this payload will never be accepted" and dropped rather than retried, while heartbeats and events use `POST` routes that were always correct — so the plugin kept reporting a healthy connection the whole time. Fixed, with a test that pins the verb per endpoint.
- **Removed the service address setting.** It is compiled in now. The server is open source, so anyone self-hosting is already building from source; as a text field it mostly offered a way to break your own sync with a typo.
- **Removed the connection overlay** and its config item. Pasting a token is now answered in the chatbox instead — accepted, rejected, unreachable, or "no token yet", which previously said nothing at all.
- **Updated the plugin description**, which still told people to enter the address that no longer exists.

The connection section is now just the opt-in switch (carrying the required warning string) and the pairing token. No new dependencies, no new permissions, and file IO is still confined to `RUNELITE_DIR`.

payload.author: Wolklaw
payload.body:
Bumped the pin from `a652df8` to `613cf30`.

No behavior change — this is documentation only, but it's directly review-relevant so I didn't want it left stale under review. A comment in `LocalSyncStore.atomicWrite()` said "the desktop app reads the offer-state file whenever it redraws the Grand Exchange slots." That was true when it was written and has been false since the desktop app I maintain stopped reading `.runelite/osrs-toolkit/` at all — but the comment stayed, and read on its own it describes exactly the arrangement this submission exists to avoid: a plugin feeding an application on the same machine.

The code under it never changed — `events/` is a network outbox (deleted once the sync service confirms it holds the event), `state/` is this plugin's own memory of the eight GE slots so a restart can still compute fill deltas correctly. Both are read by nothing but this plugin. Added a class-level doc saying that plainly, and corrected the one comment that said otherwise.

* LinkBrowser::open and Desktop::open are restricted APIs, remove your usages of them
* use of Desktop::browse is not allowed, use LinkBrowser::browse instead

payload.author: TheSpryt
payload.body:
All six done, repointed.

- `LinkBrowser::open` and `Desktop` are gone. Opening a clip and revealing it in a file manager both went with them, along with the `explorer.exe` and `open -R` subprocesses behind the latter. Clicking a clip now copies its file path to the clipboard.
- `LinkBrowser::browse` is still used for the two https links, which I understand to be the permitted call.
- `getenv` is gone. It detected Wayland to avoid a screen capture that returns black; the existing blank-frame detection already catches that case by measuring it, so nothing replaced it.
- `Runtime::availableProcessors` is replaced by fixed pool sizes.
- No interrupts: executors stop with `shutdown`, and an interrupted encode no longer re-flags the interrupt.

One thing I would rather raise than have you find: capture falls back to `Robot::createScreenCapture` when the renderer returns nothing, bounded to the client window and only while that window is focused. Happy to drop it if that is not acceptable, though it is what makes capture work on the GPU renderers.

payload.author: TheSpryt
payload.body:
Removed, and repointed.

Capture now goes through `DrawManager::requestNextFrameListener` only. The canvas bounds, the pointer position measured against the grabbed rectangle, and the blank-frame detection all went with it, the last of those because Robot fails by returning a valid all-black image rather than an error and there is nothing left to detect.
